Senses.Explanation: The graphs say a staff or cane (杖) used for propping or leaning (拄), with a noun-forming suffix (子). In the Chan record it is the monk's walking staff and a repeatedly handled teaching-seat implement. One text directly calls it an ordinary implement of a patched-robed monk (拄杖子是衲僧尋常用底). Masters pick it up, hold it, move it, plant it, lean on it, hand it over, and speak through it. Bajiao's public case gives a staff to one who has one and takes it from one who has none (爾有拄杖子，我與爾拄杖子；爾無拄杖子，我奪爾拄杖子). Another monk receives the staff and snaps it in two. The physical object is also made a participant in public address: it can distinguish the matter, teach the gate of equality day and night, or compress all the buddhas, patriarchs, and old masters into one staff. Yunmen's recorded saying has the staff become a dragon and swallow heaven and earth, then returns explicitly to “just one staff” (只是一條拄杖子). Elsewhere the staff swallows Mount Sumeru and Mount Sumeru swallows the staff, while picking it up, holding it, and moving it shakes the great-thousand world. Naming is itself repeatedly tested. Yuanwu records, “when you see a staff, simply call it a staff” (見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子). Fangrong Xi sets positive and negative naming side by side: it must not be called a staff and must not fail to be called one; calling it a staff follows another's interpretation, while not calling it a staff seeks elsewhere (不得喚作拄杖子，不得不喚作拄杖子。喚作拄杖子，則依他作解；不喚作拄杖子，則向外別求). Fenyang says recognizing the staff completes the matter of travelling on foot; Sanjiao says it sends one to hell like an arrow. These opposed formulas do not supply a second definition. The 27,727-hit base form “staff” (拄杖) and the suffixed form “the staff” (拄杖子; 4,111 hits) name the same object across these deployments.
Senses.Note: This is a corpus-wide teaching prop, not one master's idiom. The dragon saying is Yunmen Wenyan's (雲門文偃), and the give-and-take case is Bajiao Huiqing's (芭蕉慧清). Raised-case quotations keep a null `MasterName`. Family retest: the base form “staff” (拄杖) names the same object; “staff-head” (拄杖頭) names a related location or point; and the separate entry for the stick or stroke (棒) must preserve its object-versus-blow split. No evidence here warrants splitting the staff's transformations, speech, naming tests, or local equations into different referents.

Occurrences.Kwic: 芭蕉和尚示眾云。爾有拄杖子。我與爾拄杖子。爾無拄杖子。我奪爾拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wumenguan case 44, “Bajiao's Staff” (芭蕉拄杖), records Bajiao Huiqing (芭蕉慧清) addressing the assembly and giving and taking away the staff. As a raised case, it keeps a null `MasterName`.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子化為龍。吞却乾坤了也。山河大地甚處得來。只是一條拄杖子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff commentary quotes Yunmen's dragon saying and its explicit return to “just one staff” (只是一條拄杖子) in one contiguous span. As a raised quotation, it keeps a null `MasterName`.

Occurrences.Kwic: 良久，卓拄杖子，云：「拄杖子卻辯得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Wuyi Yuanlai's recorded sayings, the master pauses, plants the staff (卓拄杖子), and says that the staff can distinguish the matter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a small-gathering address, Yuanwu says, “when you see a staff, simply call it a staff” (見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子).

Occurrences.Kwic: 不得喚作拄杖子，不得不喚作拄杖子。喚作拄杖子，則依他作解；不喚作拄杖子，則向外別求。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fangrong Xi's Recorded Sayings, in “Instructions for Travelling on Foot” (行腳垂示), sets calling and not calling the object a staff side by side.

Occurrences.Kwic: 驀拈起拄杖問僧者箇是什麼僧云拄杖子師云驢年夢見
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master abruptly displays the staff and asks what it is. The monk answers “a staff,” and the response is rejected.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拈起拄杖云接取拄杖子僧接得拗作兩截師云直饒與麼也好與三十棒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master hands over the staff; the monk receives and breaks it in two, after which the master prescribes thirty blows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汾陽示眾曰識得拄杖子行脚事畢三角云識得拄杖子入地獄如箭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A case collection places opposed recognition formulas together: Fenyang says recognizing the staff completes travelling on foot; Sanjiao says it leads to hell like an arrow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲知常住性。當觀拄杖子。拄杖子吞却須彌。須彌吞却拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address directs the assembly to contemplate the staff, then makes the staff and Mount Sumeru swallow each other.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇是拄杖子。拈得．把得．動得。三千大千世界。一時搖動。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master identifies the displayed object as a staff and says that picking it up, holding it, and moving it shakes the great-thousand world.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這拄杖子晝夜為諸人說平等法門。還聞麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master says that the staff teaches the gate of equality day and night, then asks whether the assembly hears it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 過去諸佛現在諸佛未來諸佛西天二十八祖唐土六祖天下老和尚緫變成南源拄杖子去也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Nanyuan's address makes the buddhas of the three times, the Indian and Chinese patriarchs, and all old masters become his staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子是衲僧尋常用底。因什麼却道途路不得力。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff commentary directly calls the staff an ordinary implement of a patched-robed monk and asks why it is ineffective on the road.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇拄杖子是三昧你若識得拄杖子即識得天下老宿
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master locally calls this staff “complete command” (三昧) and ties recognizing it to recognizing the old masters under heaven.
